decisions.decision: Use a dedicated model service for transaction scoring
decisions.context: Each transaction needs a fraud score before authorization, with a response time of tens of milliseconds. A dedicated service gives the scoring model an online application interface. (d:1)
decisions.rationale: A dedicated service supports an online scoring path and provides an independent scaling boundary for transaction peaks. The point check returned no warnings, though it was unattested. (d:1, v:1.1)
consequences: The authorization path depends on service availability.
Model deployment and service capacity need coordination.

decisions.decision: Serve transaction scores through a real-time model service
decisions.context: Fraud scores must be available before authorization, so scheduled batch output cannot meet the brief. The workspace distinguishes distributed microservice serving from local service/API serving. (d:5)
decisions.rationale: Real-time distributed serving matches the authorization deadline and can scale apart from other application components during peaks. The point check returned no warnings, though it was unattested. (d:5, v:5.1)
consequences: The request path depends on network and service health.
Capacity planning must cover peak transaction load.

decisions.decision: Ingest transaction data as a stream
decisions.context: The system scores every incoming transaction, so inputs need to reach the ML application continuously. The workspace offers streamed, request-based, and batch ingestion alternatives. (d:7)
decisions.rationale: Continuous ingestion fits scoring each transaction as it arrives. The point check returned no warnings, though it was unattested. (d:7, v:7.1)
consequences: The ingestion path needs resilient stream handling.
The brief does not specify event ordering or replay requirements.

decisions.decision: Process transaction features in real time
decisions.context: The model must score transactions before authorization, making batch processing unsuitable for the primary scoring path. Real-time processing is an explicit workspace alternative. (d:15)
decisions.rationale: Real-time feature processing aligns with scoring before authorization. The rival point using batch processing also returned no warnings, but conflicts with the brief’s timing requirement. (d:15, v:15.2)
consequences: Feature computation becomes part of the latency budget.
Peak traffic requires processing capacity to scale.

decisions.context: The brief requires serving scores quickly and identifying which model version produced each score; it does not require the model to learn during scoring. The workspace offers batch and incremental learning. (d:19)
decisions.rationale: Batch training supports identifiable model releases while keeping training out of the transaction scoring path. This choice is an architectural inference from auditability; the workspace point check returned no warnings, though it was unattested. (d:19, v:19.1)
consequences: Model updates arrive on a training schedule.
Training data and artifacts need version records.

decisions.decision: Keep a previous model version available for rollback
decisions.context: A scoring service must remain usable during peaks, and auditors need the serving model version tied to each score. A rollback path limits the impact of a problematic release. (d:10)
decisions.rationale: Retaining a known prior version gives operators a recovery option while preserving explicit version identity. The checked point returned no warnings, though it was unattested. (d:10, v:10.2)
consequences: Each score needs the active model version recorded.
Release procedures must support switching back.

decisions.decision: Track model usage and interpretability in production
decisions.context: The brief requires auditors to know which model version and features produced each score. Production tracking includes model usage, inputs, outputs, and interpretability in the workspace. (d:22)

alternatives.label: Monitoring or logging data and predictions

decisions.rationale: This alternative most directly covers the required link among model, inputs, and outputs; the feature attribution detail in the brief calls for preserving the features used for each score. The point check returned no warnings, though it was unattested. (d:22, v:22.4)
consequences: Store model version and feature attribution with each score.
Define retention and access rules for audit records.

decisions.context: The score must return within tens of milliseconds and the service must continue working during peaks. The workspace includes prediction service performance testing as a testing alternative. (d:26)
decisions.rationale: Performance testing directly addresses both latency and peak operation. The rival point selected integration testing and returned no warnings, but does not directly test the stated response-time driver. (d:26, v:26.13)
consequences: Define latency and peak load acceptance thresholds.
Run performance checks against the deployed scoring path.

uncovered: How to guarantee availability and recover from infrastructure or dependency failures during peaks, including redundancy and failover.
How to define feature computation and storage so that the exact inputs used for each prediction can be reconstructed for auditors.
How to protect transaction data and audit records, including access control, encryption, and retention.
How to version model artifacts, feature definitions, and scoring code together.
How to define fraud model quality thresholds and decide when a model is safe to promote.
